newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Semapa expects to boost 97 sales 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Semapa expects to boost 97 sales 6 pct.

text.p: Portugal's Semapa-SGPS expects to boost its consolidated sales by around six percent in 1997 as both demand for cement and prices increase, the company's managing director told Reuters.
"We're expecting market growth of more than four percent under normal conditions," said Jose Carlos Alves in an interview. "In November we put prices up by an average 1.7 percent."
Semapa generated consolidated sales of 64.6 billion escudos ($379.3 million) last year on total production of 3.5 million tonnes of cement.
Industry analysts say the company, which has a market share of 40 percent, had increased sales by 22 percent by the end of March.
Alves said Semapa was looking to invest in cement production abroad but had no immediate plans.

"We've freed up quite a lot of cash flow and substantially reduced the liabilities we had. We're going to have to invest and we're examining the possibility of investing abroad in production," he said.
"We haven't set any targets but the price must be in line with our profits and (the company) would have to have policies that allowed us to diversify risk," he said.
Semapa's net debt stands at 24 billion escudos, down from 31 billion at the end of last year.
The company expects to invest an average 3.0 billion escudos a year in modernising and maintaining its production capacity.
Alves said Semapa would continue to pay out around 95 percent of its profit in dividends.
"In principle we'll keep the same pay-out. Semapa is a holding company and so it distributes the money it makes."
Semapa paid out a gross dividend of 140 escudos per share on its 1996 consolidated net profit of 3.66 billion escudos.
Alves declined to give a forecast for Semapa's 1997 result but Espirito Santo Research expects the company to lift its consolidated net to 4.9 billion.
At 1345 GMT Semapa's shares stood at 4,041 escudos, up 40, on volume of 400 shares.
